insights.title: OTP codes did not arrive on Oct 9, 02:00 to 10:00 UTC, so sign-ups stalled
insights.summary: Between 02:00 and 10:00 UTC on Oct 9 the OTP step stalled for about 70% of attempts, with resend rage taps and exits. Outside that window the OTP exit rate is about 5%. The pattern points to the code not being sent or received, not to how users behave.
insights.hypothesis: Between 02:00 and 10:00 UTC on Oct 9 the OTP step stalled for about 70% of attempts, with resend rage taps and exits. Outside that window the OTP exit rate is about 5%. The pattern points to the code not being sent or received, not to how users behave.
insights.recommendation: Check the SMS provider logs for Oct 9, 02:00 to 10:00 UTC, and send fresh codes to users who stalled in the window.

diagnosis.summary: Between 02:00 and 10:00 UTC on Oct 9 the share of attempts that stalled was 0.6912, against 0.05 outside that window. The pattern points to the code not being delivered.

claims.text: About 0.6912 of attempts stalled at the OTP screen inside the window.

next_steps.text: Check the SMS provider logs for Oct 9, 02:00 to 10:00 UTC.

caveats: Events alone cannot show why the code was not delivered.
reasoning: Exits at the OTP screen jump inside one time window.
The jump is the same for every persona.
That points away from user behavior.

ask.question: Why do sign-ups stall on Oct 9?
ask.answer: Between 02:00 and 10:00 UTC on Oct 9 about 70% of register and login attempts stalled on the OTP screen (about 5% outside that window). Resend taps and exits followed. The pattern points to codes not being delivered.

ask.question: Which persona drops off before a transaction succeeds?
ask.answer: Individual traders abandon Send money at the PIN confirm step about 55% of the time, against about 5% for other personas.

ask.question: Who tops up large amounts?
ask.answer: Large businesses top up above PHP 50,000 in most top-ups; every other persona stays under PHP 5,000. It is a pattern, not a problem.

ask.question: What do retail buy?
ask.answer: About 70% of retail transactions are e-load. This is expected behavior for stores that resell load.

ask.question: Which screens lose the most users?
ask.answer: Personal data loses about 18% of sessions and TIN number about 8%, steady across the whole window.

ask.question: Are the fraudster accounts a UX problem?
ask.answer: Not classified. Fraudster accounts show bursts of failed logins and up to 5 users on one device. It needs a person to review the evidence.
